title: Lecture #35: Cranial Nerves I, II, III, IV, VI
summary:
# Lecture #35: Cranial Nerves I, II, III, IV, VI

**Lecturer:** I. Kurtzer, Ph.D.
**Session:** Lecture #35

## 1. CN I - Olfactory (Slides 3-4)

*   **Function:** Smell (Visceral Sensory).
*   **Pathway:** Olfactory epithelium → Olfactory bulb → Olfactory tract → **Direct to cortex** (bypasses thalamus).
*   **Clinical:**
    *   **Anosmia:** Loss of smell.
    *   **Causes:** Head trauma (shearing of fibers), Frontal lobe tumors, **Early Parkinson's Disease** (Lewy bodies in olfactory bulbs).

## 2. CN II - Optic (Slides 5-7)

*   **Function:** Vision (Special Sensory).
*   **Pathway:** Retina → Optic nerve → **Optic chiasm** (nasal fibers decussate) → Optic tract → LGN (thalamus) → Occipital cortex.
*   **Pupillary Light Reflex (Visceral):** Retina → Optic nerve → Optic tract → **Pretectal area** → Bilateral **Edinger-Westphal nuclei** (CN III).
*   **Clinical:** Vulnerable to **vascular** (diabetes, glaucoma), trauma, MS, tumors.

## 3. CN III - Oculomotor (Slides 9-20)

### Nuclei (Slide 11)
*   **Oculomotor Nucleus:** Somatic motor (eye muscles).
*   **Edinger-Westphal (EW):** Visceral motor (pupil, lens).
*   **Location:** Rostral Midbrain (Superior Colliculus level).

### Muscle Innervation (Slide 12-14)
**Oculomotor Nucleus:**
*   **Ipsilateral:** Medial Rectus (Adduction), Inferior Rectus (Depression), Inferior Oblique (Extortion/Elevation).
*   **Contralateral:** Superior Rectus (Elevation), Levator Palpebrae Superioris (Eyelid elevation).

**Edinger-Westphal:**
*   **Ipsilateral:** Sphincter Pupillae (Pupil constriction), Ciliary Muscle (Lens accommodation).

### Branches (Slide 15)
*   **Superior Division:** Superior Rectus + Levator Palpebrae (from contralateral nucleus).
*   **Inferior Division:** Medial Rectus, Inferior Rectus, Inferior Oblique, Parasympathetics (from ipsilateral nucleus).

### Clinical (Slides 16-17)
:::correlate
**CN III Palsy**
*   **Complete Lesion:**
    *   **Ptosis** (weak Levator Palpebrae).
    *   **"Down and Out"** eye (unopposed Lateral Rectus [CN VI] and Superior Oblique [CN IV]).
    *   **Anisocoria** (dilated pupil, weak Sphincter Pupillae).
*   **Partial Lesions:**
    *   **Superior Division:** Ptosis, weak elevation.
    *   **Inferior Division:** Medial Rectus palsy, dilated pupil.
*   **Brainstem vs Nerve Lesion:**
    *   **Brainstem:** Ipsilateral lower branch symptoms (inferior division) + **Contralateral** upper branch symptoms (superior division/eyelid).
    *   **Nerve:** All symptoms ipsilateral.
:::

### Pupillary Light Reflex (Slide 20)
*   **Pathway:** Light → Retina (CN II) → Pretectal area → **Bilateral EW** → CN III → Sphincter Pupillae (both eyes).
*   **Direct Response:** Ipsilateral pupil constricts.
*   **Consensual Response:** Contralateral pupil constricts.

## 4. CN IV - Trochlear (Slides 22-27)

*   **Function:** Somatic motor.
*   **Innervation:** **Superior Oblique** (Intortion, Depression when adducted).
*   **Location:** Caudal Midbrain (Inferior Colliculus).
*   **Unique Features:**
    *   Only nerve exiting **dorsally**.
    *   **All fibers decussate** (contralateral innervation).
    *   **Smallest CN** (~2400 axons).
    *   **Longest intracranial course** (7.5 cm, vulnerable to injury).

### Clinical (Slide 27)
*   **CN IV Palsy:**
    *   **Vertical Diplopia** (worse when looking down, e.g., reading stairs).
    *   **Upward and inward eye deviation**.
    *   **Compensatory head tilt** to opposite shoulder (looks like torticollis).
*   **Causes:** Often **congenital**. Trauma (long course).

## 5. CN VI - Abducens (Slides 28-31)

*   **Function:** Somatic motor.
*   **Innervation:** **Lateral Rectus** (Abduction).
*   **Location:** Caudal Pons (Facial Colliculus).

### Clinical (Slide 31)
*   **CN VI Palsy:** **Most common** isolated ocular palsy.
    *   **Esotropia** (medial deviation, eye pulled medially).
    *   **Horizontal Diplopia** (side-by-side double vision).
*   **Causes:** Diabetes, trauma, vascular.

## 6. Conjugate Gaze and MLF (Slides 32-34, 38, 42, 44)

:::highyield
**Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus (MLF)**
*   **Function:** Coordinates conjugate **horizontal gaze** (both eyes move together).
*   **Pathway:** **Abducens nucleus** → MLF → Contralateral **Oculomotor nucleus** (Medial Rectus).
*   **Bilateral tracts** run from upper medulla to midbrain. Decussations occur immediately before entering nuclei.
:::

:::correlate
**Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia (INO) / MLF Syndrome**
*   **Lesion:** MLF tract.
*   **Presentation:** Impaired **Adduction** (medial movement) on the **ipsilateral** side during lateral gaze. Abduction is intact. Nystagmus in abducting eye.
*   **Causes:** MS (young), Stroke (older), Head trauma, Arnold-Chiari.
:::

:::correlate
**Foville's Syndrome**
*   **Lesion:** **Abducens nucleus** (not just the nerve).
*   **Presentation:** **Bilateral** impaired lateral gaze toward the side of lesion (loss of conjugate gaze). **Contralateral hemiparesis** (corticospinal tract involvement).
:::

## 7. Eye Movement Coordination (Slides 35-38)

*   **Elevation:** Superior Rectus + Inferior Oblique (both CN III).
*   **Depression:** Inferior Rectus (CN III) + Superior Oblique (CN IV).
*   **Convergence/Accommodation:** Bilateral Medial Recti + Ciliary Muscle via EW (CN III).
*   **Lateral Gaze:** Abducens (CN VI, ipsilateral Lateral Rectus) + Oculomotor (CN III, contralateral Medial Rectus) via **MLF**.
mindmap:
## Cranial Nerves I, II, III, IV, VI
### CN I (Olfactory)
*   **Smell**: Bypasses thalamus
*   **Clinical**: Anosmia (Parkinson's)
### CN II (Optic)
*   **Vision**: Retina → LGN → Cortex
*   **Light Reflex**: Pretectal → EW (bilateral)
### CN III (Oculomotor)
*   **Muscles**: 4 of 6 (MR, IR, IO, SR*, LP*)
*   **Parasympathetic**: Pupil, Lens (EW)
*   **Palsy**: Ptosis, Down-Out, Dilated pupil
### CN IV (Trochlear)
*   **SO (Superior Oblique)**: Intorsion
*   **Dorsal exit**: Decussates
*   **Palsy**: Vertical diplopia, Head tilt
### CN VI (Abducens)
*   **LR (Lateral Rectus)**: Abduction
*   **MLF**: Coordinates conjugate gaze
*   **Palsy**: Esotropia (most common)
### MLF Syndromes
*   **INO**: Impaired adduction (ipsilateral)
*   **Foville's**: Bilateral gaze palsy
